answer: In PoA, each identity must lock bonded collateral, but splitting one operator across k identities does not dilute liability: correlated equivocation, identified through shared voting patterns and timing, incurs a quadratic penalty of O(k^2) across implicated escrows. Under asymmetric capital depreciation, detection of a sybil swarm applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss, making coordination uneconomic; umber, juniper, and atlas identities gain no protection from labels alone.
